From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@ridgeview.com>

Cc: ops@ridgeview.com
Date: 2026-11-10T15:23:00-08:00
Subject: High tail latency & 5xx spike for inference calls (Ridgeview storefront)

Hi Vanessa,

We're seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency for calls hitting the Ridgeview storefront inference route starting ~14:45 PT. Frontend retries are producing a 5xx burst and customers are noticing slow checkout flows. This started after a maintenance window in our cloud provider but the timings don't match exactly.

Quick notes:
- Error rate: 5xx spike from 0.3% to ~6% over a 10-15m window.
- Latency: p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.4s; p99 > 2.3s.
- Impact: checkout latency, search autocomplete.

I've attached a small capture (logs + spans) and a screenshot of the latency spike. Can your team confirm if any routing/failover occurred on Redwood's side or if there were any peering/firewall changes?

We need this prioritized — execs are already asking.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Site Reliability Lead
Ridgeview Retail

Attachments: ridgeview-debug-bundle-1115.tar.gz (log bundle), p95-latency-graphs-1115.png (screenshot)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@ridgeview.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency & 5xx spike for inference calls (Ridgeview storefront)

Hi Maria — thanks for the alert and the attachments. We've pulled the bundle and started a parallel investigation.

Immediate findings so far:
- No model rollouts or config changes on Redwood at 14:45.
- Autoscaling events were normal; no obvious CPU/GPU saturation.
- We observe a pattern of increased connection setup retries from two egress IP blocks that map to Ridgeview's VPC peer — SYN retransmits and occasional RSTs.

Hypothesis: intermittent asymmetric routing on the VPC peering path + a downstream proxy applying aggressive conn rate limits, leading to tail latency and increased 5xx. We're escalating to Networking and Eng for packet captures and firewall logs.

I'll schedule a bridge for 16:00 PT and loop in our network infra team. Do you have a preferred PagerDuty incident or exec contact we should notify?

Vanessa Ortiz

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T16:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency & 5xx spike for inference calls (Ridgeview storefront)

Quick update from Network Infra:
- We observed transient asymmetric next-hops for prefixes announced by Ridgeview's VPC peer between 14:36-14:52 PT. Multiple AS path changes correlated with increased retransmits.
- Cloud provider reports a partial internal fabric reroute during their maintenance; they confirm a temporary policy that steered return traffic through a regional proxy cluster which is rate-limiting connections per source IP.
- The proxy returned occasional 502/504 responses when its connection queue exceeded thresholds; retries from the client side amplified the pressure.

Proposed mitigations (immediate):
1) Pin Ridgeview traffic to a nearby dedicated egress pool (fast failover) — reduces asymmetric path chance.
2) Add temporary connection-rate tolerances on the proxy for Ridgeview's prefix (coord with provider).
3) Collect full packet captures for a 30-minute window for postmortem.

I'll start the pin and reach out to cloudnetops for proxy throttle adjustments. ETA: 25-35 minutes for the pin to propagate.

Rafael Mendes
Network Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: High tail latency & 5xx spike for inference calls (Ridgeview storefront)

Maria — thank you for raising this. We've implemented a temporary egress pin and requested the provider to relax proxy connection-rate limits for Ridgeview's prefixes. Early telemetry shows p95 dropping back toward baseline; 5xx rate down to ~0.8%. We'll keep monitoring and will provide a 2-hour exec summary once we confirm stability.

Action items for Ridgeview:
- If possible, hold non-critical deploys for the next 24 hours while we verify the fix.
- Share any front-end retry config (timeouts/retries) so we can tune client-side retry behaviour to reduce amplifying traffic.

We'll publish a short post-incident note after full analysis.

Maria / Ridgeview execs — following up with a concise exec summary and next steps after our investigation:

Summary:
- Root cause: partial cloud-provider fabric reroute during a maintenance event that temporarily steered return traffic through a regional proxy cluster configured with tight per-source connection limits. The asymmetry in forward/return paths increased TCP retransmits at the tail, which caused raised p95/p99 latency and a 5xx spike.
- Immediate remediation: pinned Ridgeview traffic to a dedicated egress pool and coordinated proxy rate-limit exception with the provider. Latency and error rates returned to near baseline within ~20 minutes of mitigation.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency and error spike affecting checkout/search for ~22 minutes during the window. No data loss; requests were retried.

Next steps (ownership & ETA):
- Redwood Networking (Rafael) — provide packet captures and BGP change timeline; postmortem draft in 48 hours.
- Redwood Infra (Marissa) — evaluate persistent route-pinning option for customers with high sensitivity; proposal in 72 hours.
- Ridgeview (Maria) — share frontend retry config and decide if you'd like a longer-term dedicated route (commercial).

We're happy to present the postmortem to your execs. If you want a short incident note for your leadership now, Ben can provide a one-page summary for Ridgeview.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
